blocks.html: Imagine a food delivery backend system with all modules — authentication, browsing restaurants, and orders — built together in a single codebase.
blocks.text: Imagine a food delivery backend system with all modules — authentication, browsing restaurants, and orders — built together in a single codebase.

blocks.html: This entire application runs as one service (e.g., on a single pod).
blocks.text: This entire application runs as one service (e.g., on a single pod).

blocks.html: Problems as the system grows
blocks.text: Problems as the system grows

blocks.html: The codebase becomes very large, making it hard to debug and maintain.
blocks.text: The codebase becomes very large, making it hard to debug and maintain.

blocks.html: Different features have different loads:
blocks.text: Different features have different loads:

blocks.html: Sign-ups are rare.
blocks.text: Sign-ups are rare.

blocks.html: Browsing is frequent.
blocks.text: Browsing is frequent.

blocks.html: Orders fall in between.
blocks.text: Orders fall in between.

blocks.html: Because it’s one service, the system must scale the entire application, even if only one part (like browsing) is overloaded.
blocks.text: Because it’s one service, the system must scale the entire application, even if only one part (like browsing) is overloaded.

blocks.html: This causes inefficient resource usage and slower deployments.
blocks.text: This causes inefficient resource usage and slower deployments.

blocks.html: A small change in one feature may require re-deploying the entire app, risking downtime.
blocks.text: A small change in one feature may require re-deploying the entire app, risking downtime.

blocks.html: Solution: Microservices Architecture
blocks.text: Solution: Microservices Architecture

blocks.html: The large monolithic codebase is split into smaller, independent services, each responsible for one functionality (auth, browse, orders, etc.).
blocks.text: The large monolithic codebase is split into smaller, independent services, each responsible for one functionality (auth, browse, orders, etc.).

blocks.html: Each service runs independently and communicates with others via APIs.
blocks.text: Each service runs independently and communicates with others via APIs.

blocks.html: Services can now scale individually based on their traffic:
blocks.text: Services can now scale individually based on their traffic:

blocks.html: Auth → 1 instance
blocks.text: Auth → 1 instance

blocks.html: Orders → 3 instances
blocks.text: Orders → 3 instances

blocks.html: Browsing → 5 instances
blocks.text: Browsing → 5 instances

blocks.html: Benefits of Microservices
blocks.text: Benefits of Microservices

blocks.html: Independent scaling → Efficient resource usage.
blocks.text: Independent scaling → Efficient resource usage.

blocks.html: Faster development and deployment → Teams can work on different services without affecting others.
blocks.text: Faster development and deployment → Teams can work on different services without affecting others.

blocks.html: Improved fault isolation → One failing service doesn’t crash the entire system.
blocks.text: Improved fault isolation → One failing service doesn’t crash the entire system.

blocks.html: Easier maintenance → Smaller codebases, focused debugging.
blocks.text: Easier maintenance → Smaller codebases, focused debugging.

blocks.html: Technology flexibility → Each service can use its own tech stack if needed.
blocks.text: Technology flexibility → Each service can use its own tech stack if needed.

blocks.html: Remember that the problem with monolithic arises when codebase grows, and active users increase.
blocks.text: Remember that the problem with monolithic arises when codebase grows, and active users increase.

blocks.html: And of course microservices based architectures have challenges too, like writing more APIs for inter-service communication. Try to think more such challenges by yourself.
blocks.text: And of course microservices based architectures have challenges too, like writing more APIs for inter-service communication. Try to think more such challenges by yourself.
